english.title: Contravene an accredited person's requirement to surrender liquor - Police Reform
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), without reasonable excuse, failed to comply with a requirement imposed on you by a person accredited under the Police Reform Act 2002 to surrender **(..SPECIFY DESCRIPTION OF THE CONTAINER..) in your possession in a designated public place, namely **(..SPECIFY DESIGNATED PUBLIC PLACE..), which was, or which the accredited person reasonably believed to be, intoxicating liquor or a container for such liquor
english.legislation: Contrary to paragraph 4 of Schedule 5 to the Police Reform Act 2002, and section 12 of the Criminal Justice and Police Act 2001.

english.notes:
(i) A person accredited under the Police Reform Act 2002 who imposes a requirement on a person under Section 12(2) shall inform the person concerned that failing without reasonable excuse to comply with the requirement is an offence
(ii) The above offence relates to powers assigned to a person accredited under the Schedule 5 to the Police Reform Act 2002.
(iii) See H3869 for the comparable offence in relation to a requirement by a constable.
(iv) See also other offence wordings in relation to the duties of accredited persons:-
H4915 - failed to give name and address to accredited person - relevant offence
H4943 - fail to give name/adds to accredited person - act in anti-social manner
H4945 - contravene accredited person's requirement not to consume liquor
H4946 - fail to stop vehicle as directed by an accredited person while escorting load
H4947 - drive vehicle - fail to proceed as directed by an accredited person while escorting load
H4948 - pedestrian fail to proceed as directed by an accredited person while escorting load.

other.powersofarrest: An accredited person DOES NOT have a power of arrest or to detain - however as with any criminal offence a police officer may Arrest without warrant.
other.penalty:
A fine not exceeding level two on the standard scale.

Time limit for prosecutions:
6 months
